issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the provided solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). The template's commented Main usage also uses the three-parameter form. This inconsistency between the specification and the implementation will confuse students about the expected method signature and parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the code. Either update problem_statement.md (UML and textual description) to state acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (i.e., remove the supplier-name parameter), or change the solution and template usages to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and handle the supplier parameter appropriately. Ensure any tests and examples are updated to use the same signature.

issues.description: The problem statement (diagram and description) specifies SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — signature shown as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). The solution implementation declares acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (three parameters, omitting the supplier). This mismatch in parameter presence and ordering creates mapping confusion: students reading the diagram may implement a 4-parameter method while the provided example calls and solution use a 3-parameter variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter lists consistent. Either update the problem statement to require acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (matching the solution and example call), or modify the solution (and example calls) to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Preferably implement the latter (add supplierName as the first parameter in SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and update usages) to match the diagram and description.
